title: What do we get when we add up the counting numbers?
description: The counting numbers are added up one step at a time, and the totals are drawn as rows of dots. The rows of one, two, three and four dots stack into a triangle, which matches the totals.
teaching_notes: One idea: each running total of the counting numbers is a stack of rows of dots, so the totals fill a triangle. Watch for students who list the counting numbers again instead of their totals.

source: Figure it Out Q4 (Try This), p.8
video_script.why: The child builds running totals of the counting numbers and draws a small picture of dots that shows why the totals make a triangle.
video_script.substitution: The numbers are one, two, three and four instead of three, six, nine and twelve.
video_script.anchor: rows of one, two, three and four dots stacked into a triangle
video_script.payoff_line: Adding the counting numbers up gives the triangular numbers, and the rows of dots stack into a triangle

final_answer.value: 1, 3, 6, 10, ... the triangular numbers; rows of 1, 2, 3, 4 dots stack into a triangle
final_answer.spoken: the triangular numbers, and a triangle of dots

maths_rules: rows of 1, 2, 3, 4 dots stacked make a triangle with 10 dots
check: the dots of the triangle, 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10, match the fourth total
video_script.design: Four numbers sit in a row. A total is built under each. Then the same totals are drawn as rows of dots that stack one under the other.
